interactions.label: A patient who ingested a large dose of paracetamol 6 hours ago is alert with onl

params.question: A patient who ingested a large dose of paracetamol 6 hours ago is alert with only mild nausea. Why is it essential to start N-acetylcysteine (NAC) now rather than wait and observe?

answers.text: Paracetamol causes immediate nephrotoxicity that only NAC can prevent

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Paracetamol overdose primarily causes hepatotoxicity, not nephrotoxicity. The patient looks well because hepatic necrosis from NAPQI accumulation peaks at 72–96 hours — the deceptively normal appearance does not predict the trajectory.

answers.text: Hepatic necrosis from NAPQI peaks at 72–96 hours, and NAC is most effective within 8–10 hours of ingestion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In overdose, conjugation pathways saturate and more paracetamol is shunted through CYP2E1 to form NAPQI. Glutathione depletes silently, and liver cell destruction peaks days later. NAC replenishes glutathione and must be started within 8–10 hours for maximum efficacy.

answers.text: Paracetamol serum levels become undetectable after 8 hours, making later treatment impossible

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Paracetamol levels can be measured well beyond 8 hours. The urgency of NAC relates to preventing irreversible liver damage by replenishing glutathione before NAPQI accumulation becomes overwhelming — not to diagnostic limitations.

answers.text: Activated charcoal must be given together with NAC within the first 6 hours for either to work

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Activated charcoal and NAC serve independent purposes — charcoal reduces gut absorption if given early, while NAC replenishes glutathione to neutralise NAPQI. The urgency of NAC is its declining efficacy beyond 8–10 hours, not any dependency on charcoal co-administration.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: paracetamol hepatic necrosis peaks at 72–96 hours, long after the patient may appear well. NAC replenishes glutathione and must be started within 8–10 hours — clinical appearance is deceptive.
Well done. The key principle: a patient's appearance at presentation does not predict their trajectory — pharmacokinetics and mechanism determine outcome. NAC timing is critical.

interactions.label: A 28-year-old woman is brought unconscious after co-ingesting benzodiazepines an

params.question: A 28-year-old woman is brought unconscious after co-ingesting benzodiazepines and amitriptyline (a tricyclic antidepressant). Her breathing is adequate. Why should flumazenil be avoided in this patient?

answers.text: Flumazenil worsens the respiratory depression caused by tricyclic antidepressants

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Flumazenil reverses CNS depression — it does not worsen respiratory function. The real danger is seizure precipitation: TCAs lower the seizure threshold, and the co-ingested benzodiazepines are providing protective anticonvulsant cover that flumazenil would strip away.

answers.text: Flumazenil directly potentiates the cardiotoxic effects of amitriptyline

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Flumazenil does not directly enhance TCA cardiotoxicity. The critical risk is pharmacodynamic: by reversing the anticonvulsant effect of benzodiazepines, flumazenil unmasks the seizure-lowering properties of TCAs, potentially triggering life-threatening convulsions.

answers.text: Removing benzodiazepine anticonvulsant cover can precipitate seizures when a seizure-threshold-lowering drug is present

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. TCAs lower the seizure threshold, and the co-ingested benzodiazepines are actually providing protective anticonvulsant activity. Flumazenil competitively blocks benzodiazepine receptors, removing this protection and risking dangerous seizures — this is why it is contraindicated in TCA co-ingestion and in benzodiazepine-dependent patients.

answers.text: Flumazenil is only effective against barbiturate overdose and has no action on benzodiazepine receptors

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Flumazenil is a specific competitive antagonist at the benzodiazepine binding site on the GABA-A receptor — it was designed for benzodiazepine reversal. The contraindication here is not lack of efficacy but the risk of precipitating seizures by removing benzodiazepine-mediated anticonvulsant protection.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key principle: flumazenil reverses the anticonvulsant protection that benzodiazepines provide. In TCA co-ingestion, this unmasks the lowered seizure threshold, risking life-threatening convulsions.
Excellent clinical reasoning. Always assess for TCA co-ingestion and benzodiazepine dependence before considering flumazenil — the risk of seizures outweighs the benefit of reversal.

interactions.label: A 4-year-old child presents with irritability, vomiting, and seizures. Blood fil

params.question: A 4-year-old child presents with irritability, vomiting, and seizures. Blood film shows microcytic anaemia with basophilic stippling, and the blood lead level is critically elevated. Which chelation strategy is most appropriate?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Succimer is appropriate for moderate lead elevation without encephalopathy. This child has seizures indicating lead encephalopathy, which requires the more aggressive BAL plus CaNa₂-EDTA combination for adequate chelation and prevention of further CNS lead redistribution.

EDTA alone in severe lead poisoning can paradoxically redistribute lead into the brain, worsening encephalopathy. BAL must be given first to chelate tissue-bound lead before EDTA mobilises it from bone stores — the sequence matters critically.

Deferoxamine is the specific chelator for iron poisoning, which has a distinct mechanism (free radical generation) from lead toxicity (sulfhydryl group disruption). The clinical picture here — basophilic stippling, encephalopathy, elevated blood lead — requires BAL plus EDTA.

Correct. In severe lead poisoning with encephalopathy, BAL is administered first to chelate tissue-bound lead and prevent its redistribution into the brain. CaNa₂-EDTA is then added for systemic chelation. This sequence is critical — reversing the order risks worsening CNS toxicity.

overallFeedback.feedback: In severe lead poisoning with encephalopathy, BAL must be given first to prevent lead redistribution into the brain, followed by CaNa₂-EDTA. Succimer alone is only for moderate cases; deferoxamine is for iron, not lead.
Well done. Remember the escalation principle: succimer for moderate cases, but BAL before EDTA in severe lead poisoning with encephalopathy — the sequence prevents dangerous CNS redistribution.

interactions.label: A patient with scabies is correctly treated with permethrin 5% cream applied fro

params.question: A patient with scabies is correctly treated with permethrin 5% cream applied from the neck down for 12 hours. One month later, she presents with recurrence. What is the most likely cause of treatment failure?

answers.text: All household and sexual contacts were not treated simultaneously

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The most common cause of scabies treatment failure is reinfection from untreated contacts. All household members and sexual contacts must be treated at the same time — untreated individuals harbour mites and cause immediate reinfection, regardless of whether they are yet symptomatic.

While permethrin resistance has been reported, it is uncommon. The far more frequent cause of treatment failure is reinfection from untreated household or sexual contacts — treating only the symptomatic patient leaves the cycle of transmission intact.

answers.text: The cream was applied to too large an area of the body

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Applying permethrin to too large an area is not a cause of failure — in fact, the opposite is true. The cream must cover all skin from the neck down, since mites can burrow into clinically normal skin. Incomplete application is a treatment error, not excess application.

answers.text: Oral ivermectin should always be used as first-line instead of topical permethrin

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Oral ivermectin is reserved for crusted (Norwegian) scabies or when topical permethrin fails. Permethrin 5% cream is the first-line treatment worldwide and is effective when applied correctly with simultaneous treatment of all contacts.

overallFeedback.feedback: The most common reason for scabies treatment failure is untreated contacts, not drug resistance. All household and sexual contacts must be treated simultaneously, even if asymptomatic.
Correct. Scabies management always means treating the community, not just the individual — untreated contacts are the most common source of reinfection.

interactions.label: Topical corticosteroids can be safely used as monotherapy in herpes simplex kera

params.question: Topical corticosteroids can be safely used as monotherapy in herpes simplex keratitis to reduce corneal inflammation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false — and a critical safety rule. Corticosteroid monotherapy in HSV keratitis suppresses immune control while the virus replicates freely, leading to corneal melting and possible perforation. Steroids are only permitted in stromal keratitis under concurrent antiviral therapy (e.g. acyclovir).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Corticosteroids suppress the local immune response while herpes simplex virus continues replicating, risking corneal melting and perforation. They may be used in stromal HSV keratitis, but only with concurrent antiviral cover such as acyclovir — never as monotherapy.
